subject: Physics
topic: Heat, Calorimetry & First Law of Thermodynamics
title: Grade 9 Olympiad Heat, Calorimetry & Thermodynamics Conceptual Ontology & Dependency Graph

structural_pillars.name: Zeroth Law & Temperature as an Intensive State Invariant
structural_pillars.statement: If systems A and B are each in thermal equilibrium with system C, then they are in thermal equilibrium with each other. This establishes temperature T as a unique, transitive intensive state variable: two systems are in thermal equilibrium if and only if their temperatures are equal, dictating that heat spontaneously flows strictly from higher to lower temperature.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: T_A = T_C \land T_B = T_C \implies T_A = T_B, \quad \dot{Q}_{A \to B} > 0 \iff T_A > T_B
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Holds for macroscopic systems in thermodynamic equilibrium.

structural_pillars.name: First Law of Thermodynamics & Internal Energy State Invariant
structural_pillars.statement: Energy is strictly conserved across all thermodynamic processes. Heat Q transferred to a system equals the increase in internal energy U plus the work W performed by the system. Internal energy U is an exact mathematical state function whose cyclic integral is zero, whereas heat Q and work W are path-dependent process quantities.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: dQ = dU + dW = dU + P\,dV, \quad \oint dU = 0, \quad \oint dW = \oint P\,dV = \text{Area}_{PV} \ne 0
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Valid for closed thermodynamic systems undergoing quasi-static or irreversible transitions.

structural_pillars.name: Calorimetric Principle of Mixtures & Isolated Thermal Ledger
structural_pillars.statement: In a thermally isolated system with no non-thermal external interactions, the total heat lost by higher-temperature components equals the total heat gained by lower-temperature components until a uniform final equilibrium temperature is attained. The thermal capacity of the container vessel (water equivalent) is strictly conserved in the ledger.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: \sum Q_{\text{lost}} = \sum Q_{\text{gained}} \iff \sum_{i} m_i c_i (T_f - T_i) + \sum_{j} m_j L_j = 0, \quad W_{\text{eq}} = \frac{m_{\text{cal}} c_{\text{cal}}}{c_{\text{water}}}
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Requires an adiabatic container boundary (zero heat leak to ambient environment) at constant pressure.

structural_pillars.name: First-Order Phase Transitions & Isothermal Latent Heat Invariant
structural_pillars.statement: During a first-order phase transition (melting, boiling, sublimation) at constant pressure, thermal energy supplied does not increase particle kinetic energy (temperature remains strictly constant). Instead, latent heat breaks intermolecular potential binding networks, reorganizing the structural phase of the substance.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: Q = m L, \quad \Delta T = 0, \quad \Delta U = m L - P\Delta V
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Applies to pure homogeneous substances at invariant transition pressure.

structural_pillars.name: Ideal Gas Processes & Polytropic Heat Capacity Invariants
structural_pillars.statement: For an ideal gas governed by PV = nRT, internal energy depends exclusively on temperature (Joule's Law: dU = n Cv dT). Along any polytropic path PV^n = const, work done is the PV area integral, and the effective molar heat capacity is uniquely determined by the polytropic index n.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: dU = n C_v dT, \quad W = \int P\,dV, \quad C = C_v + \frac{R}{1 - n}, \quad C_p - C_v = R
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Applies to dilute gases obeying the ideal gas equation of state with constant specific heat ratio gamma = Cp / Cv.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: A cup of boiling water at 100 deg C contains more heat than an entire iceberg at 0 deg C.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Bodies do not 'contain heat'; heat is strictly energy in transit across a boundary due to a temperature difference. Temperature measures the average microscopic translational kinetic energy per molecule. Internal energy U is proportional to total mass: a 10,000-ton iceberg at 0 deg C contains vastly more internal thermal energy than a 200 ml teacup at 100 deg C.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Dropping a burning match (1000 deg C, negligible mass) into a bowl of cool water warms the water by less than 0.01 deg C, whereas adding 1 kg of water at 50 deg C warms it significantly.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: When water is boiling vigorously on a hot stove burner at high flame, its temperature rises above 100 deg C.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: During a first-order phase transition at atmospheric pressure, the temperature of pure water remains pinned at exactly 100 deg C. Increasing burner power merely increases the rate of vaporization (dm/dt = P_heater / L_v), consuming all extra energy to break hydrogen bonds, without raising liquid temperature.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: A digital thermocouple placed in boiling water reads exactly 100.0 deg C on low simmer and reads identical 100.0 deg C on maximum roaring burner flame.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.concept: Work and Heat as State Properties Fallacy
cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: A gas at state (P1, V1, T1) contains a specific amount of work W and a specific amount of heat Q.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Work and heat are process quantities that exist only during transitions between states; they are path-dependent line integrals. Only internal energy U is a state property. In a cyclic process returning to the initial state, Delta U = 0, but net work done W_net = oint P dV equals the non-zero enclosed PV area.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Expanding a gas from (P1, V1) to (P2, V2) along an isothermal path vs an isobaric path produces vastly different amounts of work and requires different amounts of heat, despite connecting identical initial and final states.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Because an adiabatic process involves zero heat exchange (Q = 0), the temperature of the gas cannot change.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: By the First Law, Delta U = Q - W. In an adiabatic expansion, Q = 0, so Delta U = -W. As the gas expands doing positive work against surroundings, it pays for this work by depleting its own internal energy (Delta U < 0). Since U = n Cv T, the temperature must DROP significantly: T2 = T1 * (V1 / V2)^(gamma - 1).
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Releasing compressed gas from an aerosol can or bicycle CO2 cartridge: rapid adiabatic expansion against atmospheric pressure causes the nozzle to freeze over with frost.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: When mixing hot and cold water in a metal calorimeter cup, the metal cup does not participate in heat exchange.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: The calorimeter cup is in direct thermal contact with the liquid and must reach the exact same final equilibrium temperature. Its thermal absorption Q_cup = m_cup * c_cup * Delta T = W_eq * c_w * Delta T must be included in the thermal ledger; omitting it causes systematic errors of 10% to 25% in specific heat calculations.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Calibrating a 150 g copper calorimeter cup shows that it absorbs as much heat as 14 g of liquid water (water equivalent W_eq = 14 g), significantly shifting the final mixture temperature.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: If temperature rises by 20 deg C, the rise in Kelvin must be 20 + 273.15 = 293.15 K.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: The Kelvin and Celsius degree step sizes are identical by definition: 1 K == 1 deg C. While absolute temperature requires T(K) = T(C) + 273.15, any TEMPERATURE DIFFERENCE is identical: Delta T(K) == Delta T(C). Adding 273 to a temperature difference is a severe categorical error.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Heating water from 20 deg C (293.15 K) to 50 deg C (323.15 K): Delta T_C = 50 - 20 = 30 deg C, and Delta T_K = 323.15 - 293.15 = 30 K. Delta T_C == Delta T_K exactly.
